headline: Record revenue and profit, guidance raised again
summary_short: Adobe's Q3 FY2026 revenue rose 13% y/y to a record $6.76 billion, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $6.13 (+15% y/y) and total ARR reaching $27.50 billion, as the company again raised its full-year FY2026 revenue and EPS targets.
summary_long: Record Q3 revenue of $6.76B rose 13% y/y (12% constant currency), with Total Customer Group subscription revenue up 14% y/y to $6.56B — Business Professionals & Consumers grew 16% to $1.91B and Creative & Marketing Professionals grew 13% to $4.65B. GAAP diluted EPS was $4.62 (+10.5% y/y) and non-GAAP diluted EPS $6.13 (+15.4% y/y). Total ARR reached $27.50B, up from $27.10B last quarter. Operating cash flow was a record $2.52B; Adobe repurchased $2.23B of stock and held $4.36B cash at quarter-end. RPO stood at $22.16B, with cRPO at 67% of RPO. Adobe raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $26.576B-$26.626B and non-GAAP EPS guidance to $24.45-$24.50, and guided Q4 revenue to $6.80B-$6.85B.
confidence_notes: KPI-labeling note carried over from the Q2 summary's precedent: the shard's 'eps_usd' field (6.13) is Yahoo's non-GAAP consensus figure while its prior_qq/prior_yy (4.26, 4.18) are SEC-tagged GAAP basic EPS -- a cross-basis mismatch, so no delta is computed from that field directly. Instead, Basic/Diluted GAAP EPS deltas here are computed from the EX-99.1 press release's own comparative income statement (Three Months Ended Aug 28, 2026 vs Aug 29, 2025), and the Non-GAAP diluted EPS delta is computed from the release's own Non-GAAP Results reconciliation table (6.13 vs 5.31 prior-year non-GAAP) -- same-basis (non-GAAP vs non-GAAP), so no cross-basis clearing needed. ARR delta (+1.5%) is q/q, computed by dividing this release's $27.50B against the $27.10B figure disclosed in the prior (FY2026 Q2) summary's primary source; the release itself does not give a total-ARR growth rate, only the distinct, narrower claim 'AI-first ARR grew more than 150% year over year' -- that 150% figure is NOT used as the ARR KPI's delta since it refers to a different, undisclosed-in-dollars sub-metric, not total ARR. RPO ($22.16B) has no prior comparable disclosed in this or the prior summary, so delta_basis is 'none'. Notable but unelaborated quote: CEO Narayen states 'I have confidence that Anil will build on this momentum to drive Adobe's next chapter of growth' -- the release does not name a title, role, or transition explicitly, so this summary does not assert an executive change beyond quoting the line verbatim under the 'overall' driver. Guidance and sector-specific extended metrics (ARR, RPO, cRPO, S&M/R&D % of revenue, capex, buyback, non-GAAP EPS, Q4 revenue/EPS targets) were written to the event shard per Step 3b.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes record revenue to AI-first ARR growth (>150% y/y) and reaching 1 billion monthly active users, with Business Professionals & Consumers (+16% y/y) and Creative & Marketing Professionals (+13% y/y) both contributing.
Not explained in the release beyond the underlying revenue growth; no distinct operating-margin commentary is given.
Company cites AI-first ARR growth of more than 150% y/y as a contributor, though total ARR's own q/q growth (from $27.10B to $27.50B) is not itself broken out by the release.
Not explained beyond underlying revenue and operating income growth; no distinct EPS-specific commentary is given.

Interim CFO Steve Day cites 'double-digit revenue and EPS growth' as the basis for raising full-year revenue and EPS targets; CEO Narayen highlights the 1-billion-MAU milestone and expresses confidence 'Anil' will build on this momentum, though the release does not elaborate on any executive transition.
